key_insight: Combustion instability is suppressed when the flame root overlaps spatially with the wavemaker region, suggesting localization—not just total fuel or flow changes—drives stability.
engineering_relevance: For swirl-stabilized combustors, repositioning heat release to coincide with the wavemaker can be a practical strategy to improve flame stability and reduce emissions.
method: Added low-momentum secondary methane injection through centerbody holes to redistribute heat release without strongly altering the flow.
Used fuel-staging to keep total fuel rate equivalent and isolate the effect of flame relocation.
Performed linear stability analysis to locate the wavemaker region and compare it with flame attachment position.
evidence_signal: Experiments showed an M-shaped flame transitioning to a V-shaped, attached flame, with stabilization occurring at the radial position identified as the wavemaker region.
watch_item: The conclusion depends on a specific swirl-burner configuration and low-momentum staging, so the overlap criterion may not transfer directly to all combustor designs.
paper_title: Role of flame localization in wavemaker regions on the suppression of combustion instability in turbulent partially-premixed methane flames
